answer: Each fresh identity must first walk a jade-sealed cache-line spiral: the verifier assigns pseudo-random RAM offsets and demands sequential traversal proofs where every 64-byte line read cryptographically seals the next offset in a hash chain, so skipping ahead or precomputing fails instantly. A knoll of bonded stake, say $0.40 per proof round, backs each step; if an agent stalls beyond 25 nanoseconds per line or submits a broken seal, the round aborts, the bond is slashed, and seat weight decays.
